content:
emma: Quick idea — can we make saved-query templates carry the telemetry context (sample rate, eval cohort, model pin) so when folks share a query it reproduces the same metric slices?
raj: +1 on the concept. Do we mean persisting both frontend filters and the backend telemetry predicate?
lia: Yes — frontend filters + a compact serialized predicate that the metrics API can rehydrate. We should be careful with size.
sahil: we also need to show the sampling caveat inline. Many routes use 1% sampling; people assume counts are absolute. Maybe a banner on the query view that says "Telemetry sample rate: 1%" and links to docs.
emma: good call. UX-wise I'm thinking templates vs saved queries: templates create a canonical telemetry context + default title, but users can still tweak and re-save.
raj: Implementation question: do we store the telemetry context as a versioned blob or as normalized fields? Versioned blob is easier but makes diffs opaque. Normalized fields enable query filtering in the console.
lia: normalized fields + a lightweight checksum sounds right. fields: route_id, model_id, model_version, time_range_bucket, sample_rate, custom_predicate. checksum ensures the template hasn't been mutated server-side.
sahil: For custom_predicate we need a safe expression language. Current telemetry API uses a DSL: e.g. `and(eq(route, "/translate"), ge(latency_ms, 200))`. We can reuse that but limit length and forbid expensive ops.
telemetry-bot: NOTE: New telemetry schema v2 supports tag-based filters and sample_rate metadata. See /docs/telemetry/schema-v2 for detail.
emma: UX asks: where do templates appear? Quick + templates dropdown near "Save"? Also ownership — org vs personal templates.
lia: proposal: Templates namespace = [Personal, Team, Org]. Team templates are owned by a team tag and editable by team admins. Org templates visible to everyone but editable only by admins.
raj: API shape we discussed in the last sync: POST /api/queries/templates {name, visibility, filters, telemetry_context_checksum, raw_predicate}. GET supports ?expand=telemetry_context. Any objections?
sahil: we should include an integrity check on load: if the telemetry-context references a model version no longer served, show a deprecation notice and suggest nearest compatible version.
emma: UX: deprecation banner + quick "pin to latest compatible" CTA. Also allow users to snapshot model weights metadata when creating a template for reproducibility notes.
lia: smaller detail: when exporting a template link, include ?template_ref=<checksum> so clicks always open the exact telemetry slice even if user has different default time range.
raj: ok. One more internal-api debate: do we let templates execute against live telemetry (fast) or cached snapshot (replayable)? Live is default, but offer an optional "snapshot-on-save" flag that captures counts and sample_rate at save time. Snapshots cost storage.
sahil: recommend snapshot retention for org templates limited to 30 days by default. Longer retention as an enterprise add-on.
emma: next steps: lia to prototype the dropdown and banner copy; raj to spec the API and checksum algorithm; sahil to write sampling help text and snapshot policy; I'll draft product PRD with flows.
lia: I'll drop a tiny prototype in Figma by EOD.
raj: I'll put a first-pass spec in the repo under docs/api/query-templates.md.
sahil: I'll add sampling examples and a checklist for telemetry edge-cases.
emma: thanks team — reassigning action items in the ticket. :rocket:
raj: one last nit — permissions: team templates editable by members with `team.templates.manage` scope. Add that to auth matrix.
emma: noted.
telemetry-bot: Deploy log: telemetry-api v2.3 deployed at 1968881250, feature-flag `query_template_sharing` gated.
raj: we'll gate the frontend behind that flag too.
emma: cool — closing loop, we can iterate after the prototype.
